title: Soft Pretzels, Ready‑to‑Eat, Salted, No Butter

content.title: About
content.content: Soft salted pretzels are a ready‑to‑eat baked snack made from wheat flour, water, yeast and salt. They have the classic knot shape, a tender interior and a lightly crisp exterior. The product contains no butter, making it less fatty than traditional butter‑based pretzels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels originated in Europe and were first baked in the Middle Ages.
The knot shape historically symbolized friendship and unity.
Soft salted pretzels became a popular street food in the United States in the early 20th century.
The coarse salt on the surface enhances flavor and helps keep the crust crisp.
Butter‑free versions are often chosen by people watching their fat intake.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pretzels provide quick‑digestible carbs that supply immediate energy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Absence of butter makes them less calorie‑dense compared with buttery baked goods.

items.title: Contains sodium
items.content: Salt contributes to electrolyte balance, though intake should be monitored.

items.title: Provides some fiber
items.content: Wheat flour offers a modest amount of dietary fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Easy to chew
items.content: The soft texture is suitable for people with chewing difficulties.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Pretzels contain wheat and are not suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Excessive salt may be problematic for hypertension; moderation is advised.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although low in fat, pretzels still deliver a notable amount of calories from carbs.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: As a ready‑to‑eat product, pretzels can become microbiologically unsafe if stored improperly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed straight from the package, paired with cheese, hummus, mustard, or yogurt‑based dips. They are convenient for on‑the‑go snacking or as a base for bite‑size appetizers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pretzels in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to maintain softness and prevent drying out. Discard any pretzels that become moldy or develop an off‑odor.
